text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Frederick Chiluba urges Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) members states to accelarate domestic and political reform.
- Opposition lawyers tell the supreme court that three witnesses testifying in an electoral petition against president Frederick Chiluba have disappeared.
- The Zambian and Swedish governments discuss ways in which Sweden can assist in developing Zambia's small scale enterprises.
- The Zambia Association of Manufacturers says the high level of tax evasion in the country is damaging the economy.
- Two women die in north western Zambia after taking milk and scones suspected to have been poisoned.
- A man in southern Zambian kills his brother after a heated argument over a bar of soap.
- Swedish ambassador Kristina Svenson says Sweden is working on a four-year plan to assist Zambia make the judicial system - - - -
- Cholera breaks out in the northern mining town of Chingola, with 15 victims being admitted to hospital.
